title: Soiled and clean linen: handling and storage
audience: Cleaning and service staff who collect, carry, store or handle linen in healthcare settings.
learningOutcomes: Describe how used linen is bagged and carried.
State where used linen may and may not be rinsed, sorted or washed.
Explain the storage conditions for clean linen.

instruction.heading: Policy first
instruction.body: Every healthcare facility keeps written rules on collecting, moving and storing linen. A site that washes its own linen also needs operating procedures in line with the Australian laundry standard the guideline cites. Your local procedure sets the detail for your workplace.

instruction.heading: Used linen
instruction.body: Lift soiled linen carefully so organisms are not dispersed into air or onto uniforms. Protective gear should keep exposed skin and mucosal surfaces covered. Bag linen at its point of use in the correct laundry container. Do not rinse or sort in patient zones, and never launder it in a household machine. Linen contaminated with body fluid goes into a sealed leak-proof bag for transport. Clean hands after handling used linen.

instruction.heading: Patient personal items
instruction.body: A household-type washer may take only a patient's personal clothing, never facility linen. Use a suitable detergent with hot water. Without hot water, wash one patient's load at a time. Dry those items in a dryer.

instruction.heading: Clean linen
instruction.body: Clean linen belongs in a tidy, dry space shielded from airborne particles, dust, damp and pests, and it is never mixed with soiled stock. A trolley or shelf that has carried used linen cannot be used for clean linen.

procedure: Put on the protective equipment the procedure requires before touching soiled linen.
Bag the used linen where it is used, into the correct laundry receptacle.
Close leak-proof bags around linen contaminated with body fluid.
Carry the bagged linen by the route the facility sets, keeping it clear of clean stock and staff clothing.
Clean your hands after handling used linen.
Store clean linen apart from used linen, in a dry and protected place.

workedExamples.situation: A cleaner finds a bed sheet soaked with a patient's body fluid, lying on the floor beside the bed.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What must happen to the sheet?
workedExamples.reasoning: Put on protective equipment, then bag the sheet at the bedside in a leak-proof laundry bag. Do not rinse or sort it in the room, and do not carry it loose through the corridor. Clean your hands afterwards and report the soiling as the facility requires.

equipmentAndPpe: Eye protection where splashing may occur

commonErrors.error: Rinsing or sorting used linen in the patient room.
commonErrors.prevention: Bag used linen where it is used and take it to the designated area without rinsing or sorting.

commonErrors.error: Washing facility linen in a domestic machine.
commonErrors.prevention: A household machine accepts only a patient's private items.

commonErrors.error: Storing clean linen on a trolley that has carried used linen.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep clean and used linen separate at all times.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Bagged soiled linen is handled as potentially infectious. Do not shake it, and do not carry it against your uniform.
When washing patient personal items in a domestic machine, use hot water and a suitable detergent.

qualityStandard: Used linen is placed into bags where it was used and is never rinsed or sorted within a patient zone.
Clean linen is stored apart from used linen, in a dry and protected place.
Hand cleaning is carried out after handling used linen.
documentationEvidence: Linen collection and transport record where the facility requires one
Record of any linen soiling incident and the referral
summary: Bag used linen where it is used, into leak-proof bags for body substances.
Do not rinse or sort used linen in patient areas, and do not wash facility linen in a domestic machine.
Keep clean linen dry, sheltered and apart from used linen.

knowledgeChecks.question: Where should used linen be bagged, according to the guideline?
options: In the corridor, to clear the room quickly and to save time
Into the correct laundry container, right where the linen was used.
In the staff kitchen sink and rinse it with the lunch dishes
In the nearest clean linen cupboard and stack it on the shelf

knowledgeChecks.question: Which of these is allowed for a domestic washing machine?
options: Facility bed sheets, washed on the domestic cold setting and dried on the line
A patient's own personal items, washed with a fitting detergent in hot water.
Clinical gowns from the operating suite and the scrub tops from the ward
Blankets from the emergency department and the pillows from the same bay

knowledgeChecks.question: How must clean linen be stored?
options: Beside used linen in the same cupboard as the soiled bags and the used sheets and the dirty towels
On a clean, dry shelf safe from airborne particles, dust, moisture and pests, kept well away from soiled linen.
In an open corridor where air moves freely and near the hand basin, the bins and the lift doors
Damp, so it is ready for use and folded in a pile on the floor near the door, the bins and the sink

sourceReferences: Australian Guidelines for Prevention and Control of Infection in Healthcare, B1.9 (handling of linen; patient items; B1.9.1 resources); rights: not held by user; reworded (no copying)
Source priority: the NHMRC guideline is an official Australian source. Where it conflicts with informal or in-house cleaning advice, the guideline governs the points this lesson relies on.

Australian Guidelines for Prevention and Control of Infection in Healthcare, edition note: the 2019 edition is the current edition (NHMRC, https://www.safetyandquality.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-05/australian-guidelines-for-the-prevention-and-control-of-infection-in-healthcare.pdf; CONFIRMED in the figures register, checked 2026-11-02); the uploaded copy read on 2026-11-02 is the 2010 edition, so points taken from it are UNCONFIRMED against the 2019 text. The existing aged-care and medical-equipment lessons cite the 2019 edition.
